- Acute sudden-onset inability to move the left arm since awakening ~1 hour ago with associated left facial tingling, swallowing difficulty, and progressive speech impairment; emergency ambulance arranged for suspected stroke.

  - Left-sided facial tingling began at same time as arm symptoms.
  - Patient reports speech becoming more difficult/slow during the call.
- Exacerbating/initiating/relieving factors:
  - No history of sleeping in an awkward position or different bed prior to onset.
  - No relieving factors reported.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Tingling on left side of face.
  - Difficulty swallowing (reported while trying to drink).
  - Speech slower/harder, requires more effort.
  - No pain in arm.
  - No discoloration of hand.
  - Hand/arm not cold.
  - No left leg symptoms.
  - No prior similar episodes.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No facial asymmetry reported by patient.
  - No leg weakness reported.
  - No other systemic symptoms reported.
